name: identity and session
owns: who the request claims to be, how that claim is proven, how long it lasts, and what it is allowed to do
why_in_D: Almost every web compromise ends in an identity question: whose authority is being used, and did that principal agree. Identity is the only thing that turns a read into an act. Every mechanism in this lens exists to answer that question, and every one of them can answer it wrongly.

factors.name: claim canonicalisation
factors.def: whether two spellings of the same identifier are treated as one principal, per layer
factors.observable: access granted or denied depending on Unicode normalisation or case of the identifier

factors.name: identifier namespace collisions
factors.def: whether emails, usernames and numeric ids can collide across providers or methods
factors.observable: two accounts resolving from one credential

factors.name: email normalisation practice
factors.def: which parts of an email are normalised, since providers differ on dots and plus addressing
factors.observable: an account created that aliases another's address

factors.name: uniqueness constraint location
factors.def: whether uniqueness is enforced by the store or only checked in application code
factors.observable: a duplicate created under concurrency

factors.name: registration race window
factors.def: whether check then create is atomic, which decides duplicate accounts for one address
factors.observable: two records from parallel registrations

factors.name: password policy and storage
factors.def: the algorithm, cost, salt and pepper used, and whether rehash on login is implemented
factors.observable: hash format and cost in a stored record

factors.name: credential stuffing resistance
factors.def: whether rate limiting and breached password checks exist per account and per address
factors.observable: successful logins at a rate the policy should block

factors.name: account enumeration via errors
factors.def: whether login, reset and registration reveal which accounts exist
factors.observable: response difference for existing versus absent accounts

factors.name: timing difference in credential checks
factors.def: whether the work differs measurably between existing and absent principals
factors.observable: latency distribution separation

factors.name: MFA enforcement coverage
factors.def: whether every authentication path requires the second factor, including API and legacy paths
factors.observable: a session established without the second factor

factors.name: MFA bypass via alternate flow
factors.def: whether recovery, OAuth or device trust provides a weaker path around the factor
factors.observable: a login completing through the weaker path

factors.name: TOTP window tolerance
factors.def: how many steps are accepted around now, which widens the replay window
factors.observable: acceptance of a code outside a single step

factors.name: TOTP secret storage
factors.def: whether the shared secret is encrypted at rest and readable by support tooling
factors.observable: the secret retrievable from a data path

factors.name: push notification approval semantics
factors.def: whether an approval carries context and is bound to a specific transaction
factors.observable: an approval accepted for a different request

factors.name: WebAuthn origin binding
factors.def: whether the relying party id is verified against the origin that requested the ceremony
factors.observable: an assertion accepted from an unintended origin

factors.name: WebAuthn challenge freshness
factors.def: whether the challenge is random, single use and verified
factors.observable: a replayed assertion accepted

factors.name: WebAuthn user verification policy
factors.def: whether presence alone is accepted where verification was intended
factors.observable: an assertion with presence only accepted

factors.name: credential registration trust
factors.def: whether a new credential can be added to an account without reauthentication
factors.observable: a credential added after session theft alone

factors.name: session identifier generation
factors.def: the entropy and source of the session identifier
factors.observable: predictability or repetition across sessions

factors.name: session fixation acceptance
factors.def: whether a pre-set identifier is adopted at login rather than rotated
factors.observable: a session continuing with the pre-login identifier

factors.name: session rotation on privilege change
factors.def: whether the identifier changes at login, elevation and password change
factors.observable: an old identifier valid after an elevation

factors.name: session termination completeness
factors.def: whether logout invalidates server side state, not only the client cookie
factors.observable: a captured cookie still working after logout

factors.name: concurrent session policy
factors.def: whether multiple sessions are allowed and whether one can invalidate another
factors.observable: both sessions active after a policy states one

factors.name: session storage side
factors.def: whether session state is client side and therefore forgeable if unsigned
factors.observable: modified state accepted after client side edit

factors.name: cookie scope breadth
factors.def: the domain and path a cookie is sent to, which decides whether sibling hosts receive it
factors.observable: a credential cookie sent to an unintended subdomain

factors.name: cookie prefix enforcement
factors.def: whether __Host and __Secure prefixes are used, which prevents scope widening
factors.observable: absence of the prefix on a session cookie

factors.name: cookie tossing from a subdomain
factors.def: whether a sibling host can set a cookie that shadows the parent's
factors.observable: a duplicate cookie that changes the resolved value

factors.name: same site attribute semantics
factors.def: whether Lax is sufficient for state-changing GET requests the app performs
factors.observable: a state change from a cross site top level navigation

factors.name: token lifetime and refresh coupling
factors.def: how long an access token lives and whether refresh extends it indefinitely
factors.observable: a session surviving far beyond the stated lifetime

factors.name: token storage exposure
factors.def: whether tokens are reachable from script, which turns any XSS into persistent access
factors.observable: a token readable from page script

factors.name: token binding to context
factors.def: whether a token is bound to device, address or client, which decides replay value
factors.observable: a token used from a different context

factors.name: impersonation token scope
factors.def: whether a support or admin token can act as a user and whether that is distinguishable
factors.observable: an action taken as the user with the admin's rights

factors.name: privilege escalation at the role boundary
factors.def: whether a role can grant itself or another account a higher role
factors.observable: a role change performed by an unauthorised principal

factors.name: role assignment scope
factors.def: whether roles are scoped to a tenant or resource, or global by construction
factors.observable: a role from one tenant effective in another

factors.name: permission check caching
factors.def: the window in which a cached permission outlives a revocation
factors.observable: a revoked permission still honoured

factors.name: object ownership resolution
factors.def: whether ownership is read from the record or inferred from a request parameter
factors.observable: an object treated as owned due to client supplied input

factors.name: indirect object reference predictability
factors.def: whether references are enumerable or derived from a known pattern
factors.observable: adjacent references resolving to other users' objects

factors.name: authorisation check location
factors.def: whether the check is in the handler, the model layer or only the view
factors.observable: an action allowed through a path that skips the layer holding the check

factors.name: authorisation on list versus item endpoints
factors.def: whether collection filtering equals item level checking for every record
factors.observable: a record in a list the user may not read directly

factors.name: field level authorisation
factors.def: whether sensitive fields are filtered per principal rather than per endpoint
factors.observable: a field returned to a principal that may not see it

factors.name: delegated access scoping
factors.def: whether an OAuth grant is limited to the resources and actions intended
factors.observable: an action outside the granted scope succeeding

factors.name: third party integration trust
factors.def: whether an integration's assertions are verified or accepted on the strength of the connection
factors.observable: a trusted integration acting beyond its granted rights

factors.name: API key scope and rotation
factors.def: whether a key can be narrowed, rotated and revoked independently of the account
factors.observable: a key still working after revocation

factors.name: service account credential handling
factors.def: whether machine credentials are long lived, shared between environments and stored in the repo
factors.observable: a credential valid across environments

factors.name: password reset token binding
factors.def: whether the token is bound to the account, single use and expiring
factors.observable: a token used twice or for another account

factors.name: reset link host construction
factors.def: whether the reset link host comes from the request, which turns reset into host poisoning
factors.observable: a reset link pointing at an attacker controlled host

factors.name: email change verification
factors.def: whether changing the address requires confirming the old one
factors.observable: an address changed without access to the previous one

factors.name: account recovery knowledge questions
factors.def: whether recovery relies on guessable facts, which is a social engineering surface
factors.observable: recovery completed from public information

factors.name: support assisted recovery process
factors.def: what a human operator can do to an account without cryptographic proof
factors.observable: a reset performed on request alone

factors.name: registration invitation trust
factors.def: whether an invitation carries the inviter's tenant and role, and whether that is verified
factors.observable: joining a tenant through a forged or edited invitation

factors.name: federated identity linking
factors.def: whether linking a second provider to an account requires proving both
factors.observable: an account linked without proving control of both

factors.name: just in time provisioning
factors.def: whether a first federated login creates a principal with default rights
factors.observable: a new principal with more rights than intended

factors.name: deprovisioning propagation
factors.def: the lag between disabling an identity provider account and losing access to a service
factors.observable: access retained after upstream disable

factors.name: SCIM and directory sync trust
factors.def: whether a directory sync endpoint authenticates and scopes its writes
factors.observable: a sync write accepted from an unexpected source

factors.name: anonymous and guest principal rights
factors.def: what an unauthenticated principal can do, and whether that is stated anywhere
factors.observable: a state change from an unauthenticated request

factors.name: shared link and capability URL semantics
factors.def: whether a link grants access without identity, and whether it can be revoked
factors.observable: content readable from a forwarded link after revocation

factors.name: audit attribution completeness
factors.def: whether every act records the true principal, including impersonation and automation
factors.observable: an action attributed to the wrong principal in the log

factors.name: login CSRF
factors.def: whether an attacker can log a victim into the attacker's account and observe the behaviour
factors.observable: a session established as another principal without consent

factors.name: logout CSRF and session confusion
factors.def: whether an external trigger can end or switch a session
factors.observable: a session ended by a cross site request

factors.name: remember me token strength
factors.def: whether a persistent token is separate, rotatable and revocable independently
factors.observable: a persistent token surviving password change

factors.name: identity claim propagation to downstream services
factors.def: which claims are forwarded and whether downstream services revalidate them
factors.observable: a downstream action taken on an unverified claim

factors.name: clock skew tolerance in token verification
factors.def: the allowed skew, which decides whether a just-expired token is accepted
factors.observable: acceptance of a token past its expiry by the stated skew
